title: Necessity: must have, needn't have, didn't need to
summary: Прошлое и вывод: **must have / can't have + V3** для догадок о прошлом, **needn't have + V3** (сделали зря) против **didn't need to / didn't have to** (было необязательно), а также **shouldn't have**.
ru:
## Вывод о прошлом: must have и can't have
Самый частый оборот этого юнита — логический вывод о прошлом. Если мы уверены на основании фактов, говорим **must have + V3**; если уверены, что это было невозможно, — **can't have / couldn't have + V3**:
> The ground is wet. It **must have rained** during the night. — Земля мокрая. Ночью, должно быть, шёл дождь.
> She **must have forgotten** our appointment. — Она, должно быть, забыла о нашей встрече.
> He **can't have seen** us — he walked straight past. — Он не мог нас видеть: прошёл прямо мимо.
> They **must have been** very tired after the climb. — Они, наверное, очень устали после подъёма.
Процесс в прошлом: **must have been + -ing**: He **must have been driving** very fast to get there so early.
Не путайте с обязанностью: **must have** — это вывод, а обязанность в прошлом — **had to**. Отрицательный вывод — не ~~mustn't have~~, а **can't have** (или couldn't have). (В американском английском встречается **must not have** в значении «наверное, не», но «не мог» — только **can't / couldn't have**.)

## Needn't have + V3: сделали, но зря
**needn't have + V3** говорит о том, что действие **было совершено**, хотя необходимости в нём не было:
> I took an umbrella, but it didn't rain. I **needn't have taken** it. — Я взял зонт, но дождя не было. Не стоило брать.
> You **needn't have cooked** so much; there's food left over. — Не надо было столько готовить: еды осталось полно.
Это сожаление или констатация зря потраченных усилий: I **needn't have worried** — everything went smoothly.

## Didn't need to и didn't have to: было необязательно
**didn't need to / didn't have to + инфинитив** говорит только о том, что **необходимости не было**. Сделали это или нет — решает контекст (чаще всего — не сделали):
> We **didn't need to** hurry because the meeting was postponed. — Нам не нужно было торопиться, потому что встречу отложили. (и мы, вероятно, не торопились)
> It was Sunday, so I **didn't have to** get up early. — Было воскресенье, и мне не нужно было вставать рано.
Можно сказать и о том, что сделали, но это уточняется: We **didn't need to** hurry, but we did anyway. — Торопиться было не нужно, но мы всё равно поспешили.

## Сравнение: needn't have и didn't need to
> You **needn't have come**. — Ты пришёл (а не надо было).
> You **didn't need to come**. — Приходить было необязательно. (пришёл ты или нет, не сказано)

## Needn't have и shouldn't have
Эти формы не взаимозаменяемы:
- **needn't have** — не было необходимости (зря потрачено время);
- **shouldn't have** — это было неправильно, критика: You **shouldn't have** shouted at him. — Тебе не следовало кричать на него.

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~She must have to leave early yesterday.~~ → She **had to** leave early yesterday. (обязанность) / She **must have left** early. (вывод)
- ~~He mustn't have seen us.~~ → He **can't have seen** us.
- ~~I needn't to have gone.~~ → I **needn't have gone.**
- ~~I needn't have gone to work yesterday, so I stayed in bed.~~ → I **didn't need to go** to work yesterday, so I stayed in bed. (needn't have + V3 означает, что действие было совершено)
en:
## Deduction about the past: must have and can't have
The most frequent structure in this unit. If we are sure because of the facts, we say **must have + past participle**; if we are sure something was impossible, we say **can't have / couldn't have + past participle**:
> The ground is wet. It **must have rained** during the night.
> She **must have forgotten** our appointment.
> He **can't have seen** us — he walked straight past.
> They **must have been** very tired after the climb.
For an action in progress: **must have been + -ing**: He **must have been driving** very fast to get there so early.
Do not confuse it with obligation: **must have** is deduction; past obligation is **had to**. The negative deduction is not ~~mustn't have~~ but **can't have**. (American English also uses **must not have** meaning 'probably didn't', but 'it was impossible' is **can't / couldn't have**.)

## Needn't have + past participle: done, but unnecessary
**needn't have + past participle** says that the action **was done**, although it was not necessary:
> I took an umbrella, but it didn't rain. I **needn't have taken** it.
> You **needn't have cooked** so much; there's food left over.
It expresses regret or wasted effort: I **needn't have worried** — everything went smoothly.

## Didn't need to and didn't have to: not necessary
**didn't need to / didn't have to + infinitive** only says that there was **no necessity**. Whether it was done or not depends on the context (usually it was not):
> We **didn't need to** hurry because the meeting was postponed.
> It was Sunday, so I **didn't have to** get up early.
We can add that it was done: We **didn't need to** hurry, but we did anyway.

## Comparison: needn't have and didn't need to
> You **needn't have come**. (you came, unnecessarily)
> You **didn't need to come**. (it was not necessary; we don't know whether you came)

## Needn't have and shouldn't have
- **needn't have** — it was unnecessary (wasted effort);
- **shouldn't have** — it was wrong, criticism: You **shouldn't have** shouted at him.

## Common mistakes
- ~~She must have to leave early yesterday.~~ → She **had to** leave early yesterday.
- ~~He mustn't have seen us.~~ → He **can't have seen** us.
- ~~I needn't to have gone.~~ → I **needn't have gone.**
structure:
## Формулы
| Значение | Форма | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| уверенный вывод о прошлом | must have + V3 | She **must have left**. |
| вывод о процессе | must have been + V-ing | He **must have been sleeping**. |
| невозможно | can't / couldn't have + V3 | He **can't have known**. |
| сделано зря | needn't have + V3 | I **needn't have gone**. |
| не было нужды | didn't need to / didn't have to + V | We **didn't need to** pay. |
| было неправильно | shouldn't / ought not to have + V3 | You **shouldn't have lied**. |
| обязанность в прошлом | had to + V | I **had to** leave. |

## Сравнение: форма, значение, пример
| Форма | Что было | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| needn't have + V3 | действие было, зря | You **needn't have brought** wine. |
| didn't need to + V | необходимости не было, было ли действие — неизвестно | You **didn't need to bring** wine. |
| must have + V3 | вывод: так было | She **must have brought** wine. |
| can't have + V3 | вывод: так не было | She **can't have brought** wine. |

## Отрицание и вопрос
> **needn't have** = **need not have**: I **needn't have** gone.
> **Did** you **need to** go? — No, I **didn't**. / **Did** you **have to** pay? — Yes, I **did**.
> Вывод в вопросе обычно через **could**: **Could** he have forgotten?

exercises.title: Must have, needn't have, didn't need to
exercises.instruction: Вставьте нужную форму. Допустимые варианты засчитываются.

items.text: The flight was almost empty, so I {{needn't have|need not have}} booked so early.
She {{must have|must've}} forgotten our appointment; she hasn't turned up.
He {{can't have|cannot have|couldn't have|could not have}} seen us; he walked straight past.
We {{didn't need to|did not need to|didn't have to|did not have to}} hurry because the meeting had been postponed.
You {{needn't have|need not have}} cooked so much; there's food left over.
It was Sunday, so I {{didn't have to|did not have to|didn't need to|did not need to}} get up early.
They {{must have been|must've been}} very tired after the climb.
The lights are off. They must have {{gone}} out.
She can't have {{known}} about the plan; nobody told her.
I needn't have {{worried}}; everything went smoothly.
He must have been {{driving}} very fast to arrive so early.
You needn't have {{bought}} a new suit; the old one was fine.
The window is broken. Somebody must have {{thrown}} a stone at it.
We needn't have {{taken}} warm coats; it was quite mild.

items.q: The ground is wet. It ___ during the night.
I took an umbrella, but it didn't rain. I ___ it.
She has no idea about it; she ___ the news.
items.why: Отрицательный вывод → **can't have + V3**. **must have heard** противоречит первой части предложения.

items.q: Yesterday was a holiday, so we ___ go to work.
items.why: Не было необходимости → **didn't have to + инфинитив**.

items.q: You ___ shouted at him; he's only a child.
items.why: Критика за неправильное действие → **shouldn't have + V3**.

items.q: Why was the bank closed? There ___ a problem.
Tom ___ have missed the train; he's always on time.
items.why: Отрицательный вывод: **can't have + V3**. **didn't have missed** невозможно, а **needn't have missed** значило бы «опоздал зря».

options: Вы пришли, но это было необязательно.
items.why: **needn't have + V3** — действие было, а необходимости не было.

options: Приходить было необязательно; пришли ли вы, не сказано.
items.why: **didn't need to** не говорит, совершено ли действие.

items.q: Какое предложение показывает, что действие было сделано?
items.why: Только **needn't have + V3** подразумевает, что действие состоялось.

options: You didn't need to say that.
She must have to leave early yesterday.
She must have left early yesterday.
She had to leave early yesterday.
items.why: Обязанность в прошлом — **had to**, вывод — **must have left**.

items.q: Какое предложение значит «он не мог нас видеть»?

exercises.title: Перепишите
exercises.instruction: Перепишите предложение, используя слово или конструкцию в скобках.

items.prompt: I'm sure that she missed the bus. (must have) → She ...
answers: She must have missed the bus.

items.prompt: It was unnecessary for him to take a taxi, but he took one. (needn't have) → He ...
answers: He needn't have taken a taxi.
He need not have taken a taxi.

items.prompt: It's impossible that they heard the alarm. (can't have) → They ...
answers: They can't have heard the alarm.
They cannot have heard the alarm.
They couldn't have heard the alarm.
They could not have heard the alarm.

items.prompt: It wasn't necessary for us to pay for the tickets. (didn't have to) → We ...
answers: We didn't have to pay for the tickets.
We did not have to pay for the tickets.

items.prompt: I'm sure he was joking. (must have been) → He ...
It was a mistake for her to sell the house. (shouldn't have) → She ...
answers: She shouldn't have sold the house.
She should not have sold the house.
She ought not to have sold the house.
She oughtn't to have sold the house.

items.prompt: Explain why a friend did not come to your party (must have / can't have).
items.sample: He must have been busy; he can't have forgotten, because I reminded him the day before.

items.prompt: Write about something you did but needn't have done.
items.sample: I needn't have left home so early; the train was late.

items.prompt: Write about something you didn't need to do last week.
items.sample: I didn't need to cook last week because we ate at my parents' house.

items.prompt: Write about something you shouldn't have said or done.
items.sample: I shouldn't have shouted at my brother.

items.prompt: You see a wet street and open windows in the morning. What must have happened?
items.sample: It must have rained during the night.

items.prompt: Your flat is untidy and the door was open. What must have happened? Use must have / can't have.
items.sample: Someone must have broken in; it can't have been the wind.
